operative_clause_inventory.text: Instructions to the Commanders of armed vessels belonging to the United States; given at Washington on 18 February 1802.

Cites the statute for protection of U.S. commerce and seamen against Tripolitan cruisers, permitting arming and manning armed vessels and presidential instructions to public-vessel commanders to subdue, seize and make prize vessels/goods/effects belonging to the Bey of Tripoli or his subjects.

'In pursuance of the said statute' commanders are 'authorized and directed to subdue, seize, and make prize' of vessels, goods and effects belonging to the Bey of Tripoli or his subjects, and bring/send them into port for proceedings according to law.

historical_inclusion_proposal.reason: A page formatted as a public presidential instruction to a class of U.S. armed-vessel commanders, expressly 'by command of the President,' gives substantive prospective authorization/direction, and is explicitly grounded in statute. On present evidence it is more than a private letter and fits the proposed broad issuance-attributable-to-President historical unit. The official print/copy's exact documentary status and how the project's selected Lord-based authorship convention treats a printed command remain a residual identity question for adjudication; recommendation is limited to historical inclusion as an instrument candidate, not original-authentication or lifecycle certification.

issuer_capacity.finding: The four retained LOC master manuscript pages are a signed presidential instruction from Thomas Jefferson to Captain Meriwether Lewis. Page 4 closes 'Given under my hand at the city of Washington this 20th day of June 1803' and bears 'Th. Jefferson Pr. U.S. of A.' The LOC transcription identifies the manuscript as in Jefferson's hand. Recipient is a U.S. Army captain and presidential secretary, expressly appointed to execute Congress's expedition purpose.
issuer_capacity.confidence: high for president-authored/signed instruction and recipient/capacity.

date_verified.finding: Original manuscript p.4 explicitly dates the signed instrument June 20, 1803. The editorial transcription's heading uses '[ante June 20 1803]' and its note says dateline/signature were added later, in Jefferson's own hand, after the body was sent to Lewis, Madison, Lincoln and Gallatin for comments in April. This supports an April drafting/review phase and a June 20 signed date; it does not prove dispatch occurred on that date.
date_verified.qualifier: signed date verified from manuscript; body drafted and circulated for comments in April; dispatch date not separately shown.

operative_clause_inventory.text: Address to Lewis as captain; states he is appointed to execute objects in Jefferson's confidential Jan. 18, 1803 message and congressional act; directs preparation of instruments, supplies, arms, boats, medical/provision stores with War Department assistance; authorizes recruitment of 10-12 military attendants by voluntary agreement and vests command powers provided by law.

Specifies the expedition's geographical mission: explore the Missouri and principal stream(s) offering practical communication to the Pacific; gather observations and report on geography, waterways, resources, inhabitants and routes; covers conduct and diplomatic engagement with Native nations and other peoples, with concrete limits and authorized presents/commerce.

Provides command continuity: if Lewis dies, he may name in his own signed instrument the successor from the party; that successor receives the same powers and may name successors in turn, whose authority vests on predecessor's death. This is a contingent standing delegation internal to the expedition, expressly included in the signed order.

historical_inclusion_proposal.reason: This is an individually signed, formally addressed presidential instruction appointing and empowering an officer to execute a congressionally authorized federal mission. It contains operative directions, statutory/office authority and a contingent succession mechanism; identity is not merely a private presidential letter or an editor's label. Under the project’s proposed broad historical unit (presidentially attributable issuance), recommend count as one instrument, subject to owner’s final historical boundary adjudication.
historical_inclusion_proposal.instrument_identity: One four-page signed instruction to Lewis; April circulated body and June signed dateline belong to one instrument, not separate issuances.
historical_inclusion_proposal.possible_first_cause: Not researched; assignment concerns inclusion only. The mission's completion or Lewis's death is not assumed to have ended every delegated clause.
historical_inclusion_proposal.duplicates: No full Lord/bibliography crosswalk performed. Do not treat transcript's prior April circulation, editorial heading, or manuscript copies sent for comment as extra orders.

residuals_and_contrary_evidence: LOC transcription heading is 'ante June 20, 1803' and footnote says date/signature were later added than April body; source page p.4 resolves signed date but not actual mailing date.

The instruction is a mission-specific presidential communication, not a document labeled 'Executive Order'; Lord's editorial convention can exclude private letters and distinct military orders. operative_clause_inventory.text: The Executive wants Wilkinson to seek a written convention/temporary line between American and Spanish troops, and says no military hostility should occur absent actual hostile acts; if attack occurs, hold defensive positions.

operative_clause_inventory.page: 2-4, heading and numbered proposed convention clauses I-VI plus handwritten revisions
operative_clause_inventory.text: Proposed terms include immediate suspension of hostilities, temporary separation line, limits on civilian crossing, no new military establishment, non-interference with Indigenous nations, release/return of captives, and ratification/revocation notice. Explicitly framed as 'Heads of a Convention to be proposed' rather than itself an executed agreement/order.

Conditional directions: if convention/temporary line is rejected, take best measures to protect/defend settlement in its current position; if no hostilities have begun, remain strictly on defensive and do not cross the Sabine River. Further direction conditions a suspension of hostilities and possible disposition/withdrawal of forces on Spanish agreement and on the parties' conduct. Exact text partly canceled/interlineated and is not fully legible.

historical_inclusion_proposal.reason: Source supports a substantive presidential-executive communication with proposed and conditional commands to a military commander, but the retained seven-page packet's boundaries and issuance status are unclear: Nov. 8 report, Nov. 5 draft convention, conditional instruction pages, and envelope/address leaf are assembled together; no signed dispatch/complete cover or addressee authentication is visible in reviewed facsimiles. The project’s proposed historical convention also distinguishes ordinary presidential letters and distinct military orders, leaving classification unresolved. Do not count draft convention clauses as themselves operative or count attached pages as separate orders.
